title: Bath Store and More
text:
Personal projects


  Web design · 2025
  Bath Store and More
  A full website built for Bath Store and More, a Dublin-based bathroom design and installation company offering luxury bathroom solutions.
  
    WordPress

      Year

  About the project
  Bath Store and More is a Dublin-based bathroom design and installation company helping homeowners transform their bathrooms into luxury spaces. The business needed a professional website to showcase their portfolio, share brochures, highlight showrooms, and make it easy for customers to get a quote.
  This was my second WordPress and Elementor Pro build. Having gone through the learning curve with VIP Ireland, the process was noticeably smoother. I was more confident in the platform, faster with the layout tools, and better at making design decisions from the start.





  What I built
  
    
      Pages
      Home, Portfolio, About, Brochures, Showrooms, Contact, Blogs
    
    
      Tools used
      WordPress, Elementor Pro, custom CSS
    
    
      Focus areas
      Portfolio presentation, brochure downloads, quote request flow, mobile responsiveness
    
    
      Outcome
      Fully live professional website at bathstoreandmore.ie
    
  





  Reflection
  Compared to VIP Ireland, this project felt like a different experience entirely. The foundational knowledge I had built on the first site meant I could focus more on design quality and less on figuring out the tools. The result is a richer, more visual site with a stronger layout and better overall user experience.
  Building two client sites back to back gave me a real sense of progression. I can see the improvement between the two projects and it has given me confidence to take on more complex web design work going forward.




Visit bathstoreandmore.ie

title: Future Goals
text:
I'm graduating in April 2026 with a clear sense of where I want to go, not just professionally, but personally. Here's what I'm working towards.




Short term
Business analyst in the gaming industry
My goal after graduating is to work as a business analyst, ideally within the gaming industry. It's a sector I find genuinely exciting: fast-moving, data-driven, and creatively ambitious. I want to be part of a team where analytical thinking shapes real product decisions.

Working abroad in London
London is one of Europe's biggest hubs for tech and gaming companies. Moving there after graduation is a goal I'm actively working towards. The exposure, the network, and the pace of the industry there is exactly the environment I want to grow in early in my career.

title: Superdry strategic analysis
text:
Academic projects


  Group project · 2025
  Superdry strategic analysis
  A strategic review of Superdry conducted as part of a consulting simulation for the BAA1019 Business Strategy module at DCU, prepared by A & A Consultancy, Group BS1.
  
    Business Strategy
    PESTEL
    Porter's Five Forces
    SWOT
    Group project
  
  
    
      Year
      2025
    
    
      Module
      BAA1019
    
    
      Type
      Group · 6 members
    
    
      Word count
      4,101
    
  



  About the project
  As part of the BAA1019 Business Strategy module, our group of six acted as a strategy consultancy, A & A Consultancy, tasked with producing a full strategic review of Superdry. The report examined how the brand captured value in its early years, why it declined through overexpansion and brand dilution, and what strategic interventions could restore its competitive position.
  The analysis followed a structured consulting process: Orientation, Diagnostics, Intervention, and Evaluation, applying frameworks including PESTEL, Porter's Five Forces, SWOT, RBV/VRIO, and the Strategy Diamond to build a comprehensive picture of Superdry's strategic trade-offs.





  Key findings
  
    
      Core problem
      Brand dilution and a shift to a discount-driven volume model eroded Superdry's premium differentiation
    
    
      Frameworks used
      PESTEL, Porter's Five Forces, SWOT, RBV/VRIO, Strategy Diamond, ERRC Grid
    
    
      Recommendations
      Rebrand around durability and responsibility, shift to digital-first DTC model, restructure the organisation
    
    
      My role
      Associate Director. Led analysis and synthesis sections, contributed to diagnostics and recommendations
    
  





  Reflection
  This was my first experience working in a structured consulting format. Applying real strategic frameworks to a live business case made the theory feel tangible and practical. The group dynamics were challenging at times, particularly around the presentation, but working through those difficulties strengthened both the final report and my ability to collaborate under pressure.

title: ePortfolio (this website)
text:
Academic projects


  Academic project · 2025
  ePortfolio (this website)
  A professional ePortfolio designed and built from scratch as part of my BSc in Business Studies at Dublin City University, using Quarto, custom SCSS, and GitHub Pages.
  
    Quarto
    HTML
    SCSS
    Git
    GitHub Pages
  
  
    
      Year
      2025
    
    
      Module
      BAA1027
    
    
      Type
      Individual
    
    
      Live site
      alekslupa.github.io
    
  



  Project goal
  Although I had prior experience building websites using WordPress and Elementor Pro for freelance clients, this project was a completely different challenge. WordPress abstracts most of the underlying code, whereas building with Quarto required working directly with markup, SCSS, YAML configuration, and Git from the ground up. It was my first time working in this kind of development environment.
  The goal was to build a fully functional, publicly hosted professional ePortfolio that demonstrates technical ability across web development, version control, and design, while also serving as a genuine platform to showcase my academic and personal journey.





  What I built
  The site covers every area of my profile: a custom landing page with hero section and project previews, a detailed about page pulling in my real work experience and education, an achievements page listing all 30 Kubicle and 9 LinkedIn Learning certificates, individual project pages for each piece of work, a future goals page, and a fitness journey timeline with alternating photo and text entries.
  Every page uses custom SCSS with no reliance on default Quarto theming. All styles are managed centrally in a single stylesheet, with consistent typography, spacing, card components, timelines, and responsive layouts throughout.





  Skills developed
  
    
      Framework
      Quarto and YAML configuration
    
    
      Styling
      Custom SCSS and responsive CSS layouts
    
    
      Version control
      Git branching, commits, and pull requests
    
    
      Deployment
      GitHub Pages with docs folder setup
    
    
      Design
      UI layout, typography, and component design
    
    
      Content
      Writing professionally for a public audience
    
  





  Challenges
  
    
      01
      
        Learning Quarto from scratch
        Unlike WordPress where the platform handles most of the structure, Quarto required me to understand how .qmd files, YAML configuration, and the rendering pipeline all connect. Coming from a visual page builder background, this was a significant shift in how I thought about building a website.
      
    
    
      02
      
        Custom SCSS without a design system
        Building a consistent design language from scratch, with no existing framework to lean on, required a lot of planning. Getting components like the timeline, card grid, and skill bars to look right across both light and dark mode took several iterations.
      
    
    
      03
      
        Git and GitHub Pages deployment
        This was my first project using Git for version control. Managing commits, configuring the output directory, and getting GitHub Pages to serve the rendered docs folder correctly required careful debugging before the site went live successfully.
      
    
  





  Reflection
  This project pushed me further technically than any other module assignment. I already knew how to build websites through WordPress, but this was a completely different experience. Working directly in code, managing a project through Git, and deploying to a live URL through GitHub Pages gave me a much deeper understanding of how the web actually works under the hood.
  More than the technical skills, it taught me how to think about design, structure, and user experience when building something entirely from scratch. Having prior web design experience helped with layout instincts, but everything else had to be learned from the ground up.

title: PriceBeo
text:
Academic projects


  Capstone project · 2025
  PriceBeo
  A real-time barcode-scanning grocery price comparison app for the Irish market, developed across four assignments as part of the New Enterprise Development module (BAA1003) at DCU. Pitched in a mock Dragons Den to a panel of investors.
  
    New Enterprise Development
    Dragons Den pitch
    Group project
    Product strategy
  
  
    
      Year
      2025
    
    
      Module
      BAA1003
    
    
      My role
      CTO
    
    
      Team
      Group 38 · 5 members
    
  



  
    80
    Survey respondents
  
  
    €100K
    Investment asked
  
  
    20%
    Equity offered
  
  
    5
    Major retailers covered
  





  About the project
  PriceBeo is a mobile app that lets users scan any product barcode in-store and instantly compare prices across Ireland's five major retailers: Tesco, Dunnes Stores, Lidl, Aldi, and SuperValu. With grocery prices up 27% since 2021 and limited tools available to Irish shoppers, the app targets a clear and validated market gap.
  As CTO, my role was to lead the technical vision and strategy for the platform. This meant understanding how the technology worked, making informed decisions about architecture and data infrastructure, and working closely with outsourced developers and technical advisors to bring the product to life. I bridged the gap between the business team and the technical side, ensuring our solution was feasible, well-structured, and clearly communicated.





  The four assignments
  
    
      
        Assignment 1
        Initial concept and idea validation
        BAA1003
      
      
        Developed the initial PriceBeo concept, defined the problem statement around grocery price transparency in Ireland, and outlined the core app idea. Established the team structure with defined roles including CEO, COO, CFO, CMO, and CTO.
      
    
    
      
        Assignment 2
        Feasibility study and value proposition
        BAA1003
      
      
        Conducted a full feasibility study covering industry attractiveness, product and technical feasibility, organisational feasibility, and financial projections. Validated the concept through an 80-person survey, 4 in-depth interviews, and consultation with Quidu, Ireland's leading grocery price comparison platform. Developed a Value Proposition Canvas, customer empathy maps, and outlined the technical architecture. Produced a full financial model including startup costs of €157,720, a 5-year plan, and breakeven analysis.
      
    
    
      
        Assignment 3
        Marketing campaign and video
        BAA1003
      
      
        Developed a full marketing strategy for PriceBeo covering the 2027 to 2028 period. Designed five integrated initiatives: a Scan It and Prove It social media challenge, a quarterly Grocery Transparency Report, strategic trust and advocacy partnerships, an Ireland's Savings Movement community campaign, and a retention and lifecycle marketing strategy. Also produced a marketing video as part of the submission.
      
    
    
      
        Assignment 4
        Business report and Dragons Den pitch
        BAA1003
      
      
        Produced a full investor-ready business report and pitched PriceBeo in a mock Dragons Den to a panel of lecturers acting as investors. The pitch covered the problem, solution, market opportunity, competitive landscape, financial projections, and a funding ask of €100,000 for 20% equity. Projections showed revenue growing from €99,440 in Year 1 to €938,625 by Year 3, with profitability from Year 2.
      
    
  





  My role as CTO
  
    
      Technical vision
      Led all strategic technical decisions including architecture, data infrastructure, and system design
    
    
      Outsourcing
      Collaborated with external developers and DCU computer science advisors to deliver the product
    
    
      Bridging the gap
      Translated technical concepts for the business team and ensured feasibility at every stage
    
    
      Pitch contribution
      Presented the technical architecture and product infrastructure to the Dragons Den investor panel
    
  





  Reflection
  PriceBeo was the most demanding and rewarding project of my degree. Working across four assignments over the full academic year, the project developed my ability to think like a founder: validating a real problem, designing a technically sound solution, building a financial model, and pitching to investors under pressure.
  As CTO, my role was to lead the technical vision and strategy for the platform. This meant understanding how the technology worked, making informed decisions about architecture and data infrastructure, and working closely with outsourced developers and technical advisors to bring the product to life. I bridged the gap between the business team and the technical side, ensuring our solution was feasible, well-structured, and clearly communicated.
  The Dragons Den pitch was a genuine test of confidence and clarity under pressure, and the full project experience gave me a much deeper understanding of what it takes to build and launch a technology product from scratch.
